title: Two-finger gripper for a FANUC robot
summary: A parallel two-finger end-of-arm gripper, with manufacturing drawings and an assembly review.
work: Designed the gripper and its parametric parts in SolidWorks, including assembly interfaces and motion constraints.
Prepared manufacturing drawings with GD&T, selected fits, positional tolerances and surface-finish requirements.
Reviewed the design using Design for Assembly principles and reduced the required assembly steps from nine to six.

title: Structural component material optimization
summary: A comparison of six candidate materials against a steel baseline to assess stiffness, mass and manufacturing constraints.
work: Compared six candidate materials with a steel baseline using Ansys Granta and Ashby material-selection charts.
Evaluated specific stiffness, component mass, machinability, corrosion behaviour, thermal resistance and relative cost.
Shortlisted two aluminium-alloy options that could provide the required stiffness at a lower mass.

title: Sensor-based obstacle avoidance
summary: A mobile platform using proximity sensors for real-time obstacle detection and path correction.
work: Integrated ultrasonic and IR proximity sensors on a mobile platform.
Developed decision logic for real-time obstacle detection and path correction.
Tested the platform across three surface types, with a reported avoidance response within 120 ms.

title: Collective perception in a robot swarm
summary: A decentralized swarm that identifies the dominant floor colour and works toward a majority consensus.
work: Developed a decentralized robot swarm to identify the dominant floor colour.
Implemented collective decision making so the swarm could converge toward a strong majority consensus without centralized control.

title: Fault-tolerant jump counter on T-Watch
team: Shubham Jadhav and Shanal Orin Dsouza
summary: A team project to count skipping-rope jumps and track workout duration on a T-Watch, with pause/resume controls and an inactivity timeout.
work: Implemented jump detection using Z-axis IMU acceleration, with take-off and landing thresholds and a minimum air-time check.
Added a workout timer, a start countdown, pause/resume and reset controls, and vibration feedback.
Automatically paused the workout after 15 seconds without a detected jump.
Presented the design using Hanmer’s Minimize Human Intervention and Correcting Audits patterns, with two recorded demonstrations.
focus: Jump-event validation, workout state control and automatic inactivity handling
limitations: Z-axis sensing is affected by watch tilt and loose wearing. Arm movements can produce false detections. The design uses one IMU, without sensor redundancy or orientation compensation.
